paper_id: Liu et al. - 2014 - Self-Diagnosis for Detecting System Failures in Large-Scale Wireless Sensor Networks
title: Self-Diagnosis for Detecting System Failures in Large-Scale Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: Sink-based diagnosis causes huge communication overhead and obtains incomplete information due to unreliable wireless links
problem_framing: How to enable single sensors with narrow local scope to cooperatively diagnose failures without centralized control
key_insight: Encode diagnosis process as FSM state transitions; nodes transit state based on local evidence and propagate only the small current state
method_signature: FSM-based fault detectors that travel among nodes, transiting states via local evidence until Accept state is reached
evaluation_criteria: Detection ratio, false alarm ratio, and traffic overhead (diagnosis traffic / total traffic)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Sink must tolerate inconsistent results from different nodes; diagnosis messages themselves can be lost due to congestion
evidence_for_taste: sink often obtains incomplete and suspicious information
problematic sensors themselves are usually incapable
a sensor only has very narrow scope on the system state
our approach can pinpoint the root causes from the local evidences only
fault detectors are not intended for single node
different nodes have different views of the network
thinking_moves: 把 sink 拉模型反转为节点推模型
把诊断问题形式化为状态机状态转移
用 CUSUM 加 bootstrap 做变化点检测来触发诊断
开放框架: 新故障类型可通过传播新检测器解决
邻居协作弥补死亡节点无法自报的问题
